To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
innovativeness is a critical component of market orientation and that it is related to organizational learning and adaptation.

higher levels of market orientation and organizational innovation are related to higher levels of innovating, which are associated with a culture that is characterized by high levels of learning and development and participative decision-making.

(a) higher levels of innovational culture are associated with higher levels of organizational learning, (b) higher levels of organizational innovativeness are positively associated with the capacity to implement innovations successfully, and (c) higher levels of innovative culture are associated with greater emphasis on learning and development and greater emphasis on participative decision making
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of organizational learning in the innovation process.
the relationship between organizational learning, innovation, and market orientation.
the role that innovation plays in the market orientation-organizational learning relationship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study provide empirical support for the conceptual model and suggest a number of important relationships among market orientation, innovativeness, and organizational learning.
the results of the study support the conceptual model and the hypotheses.
the results support the notion that innovation is an essential part of a market-oriented culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the market orientation of an organization, the innovativeness of an organization, and the organizational learning orientation of an organization all influence the number of innovations successfully implemented by an organization.
the more innovative a firm is, the more market oriented it tends to be and, in turn, the more successful it is.
innovation, market orientation and organizational culture are all related to organizational learning and adaptation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the market orientation construct is not a complete explanation for how organizations adapt to changing environments, develop competitive advantage, and achieve high levels of performance.
market orientation and organizational innovation are not independent constructs, but they are interdependent constructs.
market orientation and innovation are closely linked.
